story_text.value:
A month ago, I shared mini-AGI, an experiment in training a byte-level, continually learning language model from scratch on a single 8 GB laptop GPU (an RTX 3070). To recap the setup briefly: it completely decouples model size from VRAM by paging experts to and from an NVMe drive (currently 397 experts / 1.26B total parameters on disk, with only 32 resident / ~109M active in 5.1 GB of VRAM). It trains on a single stream at batch 1, with the attention/embedding trunk learning rate dampened to 0.1x to mitigate catastrophic forgetting.

The training is still going and went only through ~35% of the training corpus selected at the beginning of the run (about 8GB in total). Here is the current status:

1. enwik9 (First 10^9 bytes of English Wikipedia):

    Model               Params   Data Read       Cost     enwik9 (bits/byte) ↓

    Llama-3.2-1B        1.23B    36 TB (9T tok)  ~$900k   0.68
    Chinchilla 1B       1.00B    5.6 TB          ~$68k    0.90
    GPT-2 XL            1.56B    40 GB           ~$43k    1.07
    GPT-2 Large         0.77B    40 GB           ~$21k    1.12
    mini-AGI (online)   1.26B    2.8 GB          ~$56     1.14
    GPT-2 Medium        0.35B    40 GB           ~$10k    1.17
    mini-AGI (dynamic)  1.26B    2.8 GB          ~$56     1.23
    mini-AGI (frozen)   1.26B    2.8 GB          ~$56     1.29
    GPT-2 Small         0.12B    40 GB           ~$3k     1.33
2. PG19 (100 Project Gutenberg books, 41 MB test split):

    Model               Params   Trained On        Cost    PG19 (bits/byte) ↓

    MambaByte-972M       0.97B   75 GB (PG19)      ~$4k    0.883
    MegaByte-1B          1.02B   80 GB (PG19)      ~$1.6k  1.000
    Transformer-320M     0.32B   80 GB (PG19)      ~$1.6k  1.057
    mini-AGI (online)    1.26B   2.8 GB (0 PG19)   ~$56    1.447
    mini-AGI (frozen)    1.26B   2.8 GB (0 PG19)   ~$56    1.995

    The published models were trained on PG19's own training books, 75 to 80 GB of them, and are scored on more books like those. mini-AGI has never been trained on PG19 and has read no Victorian novels, so for it these books are completely out of its domain.
There are more details in the repository. The most important part is a difference between "frozen" and "online" attempts where we allow the model to specialize on the task as it goes through the evaluation dataset. Clearly showcasing the power of continual learning regime simply unavailable for any other typical LLM.

Full methodology, and replication code is in the repo: https://github.com/volotat/mini-AGI

Intermediate weights snapshot on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/Volotat/mini-AGI-undertrained

story_text.value:
I'm building Multipeer, a desktop app for running agents, tools and working wth teammates on one shared canvas.

I often have several agent sessions open at once, but they're all scattered across terminals. It was also hard for my co-founder to see what my agents are doing or jump in to work together. So We built the solution to our own problem. And now we're releasing it to the world.

It's a macOS app for now (soon on Windows and Linux). You can invite your teammates over a local network or over the internet. They can follow your view and, if you allow them, they can also take control of your terminal and claude code/codex sessions.

The app is still early, and I'm also releasing the iPhone/Android app soon to remotely control everything on your canvas.

I'd would like to get feedback from the HN community! If there's any features you'd like to see, please contact me via: shyam@multipeer.sh, we build really fast. I'd love to talk to everyone of you and work on your feedback!

Thanks!

story_text.value:
Encarta is super nostalgic, and I was surprised it wasn't available to use online. So I embarked on the difficult task of making it so.

The way this works is the most convoluted, nonsense and brittle system ever... but it works as a statically hosted gh-pages site!

Please note: All the material on this site is freely available through the internet archive (see github readme)

Github repo -> https://github.com/benwinding/encarta_95_web

story_text.value:
I've been training mostly outside for over a decade. I spent a decent amount of time in front of a screen, so it's usually a good opportunity to get some sun and fresh air.

I used https://calisthenics-parks.com/ for most of that time, but it was always slow and clunky. And then they took the site offline.

So, I built this: a map of 25k+ outdoor gyms, pull-up bars, and other exercise stations all over the world.

Maybe that's helpful to others.

story_text.value:
Launched a beta/buggy version of the SDK for web bot auth, and it's live at https://messh.io

Inspired by https://datatracker.ietf.org/wg/webbotauth/documents/

While solving this, I realized it solves the hassle of adding SSH keys, the overhead of copy-pasting n number of times to a remote server; just do

messh add amul

It will automatically search for Amul's public key and add it to my server

Do try if you find it interesting. But the main product aim is to solve web bot auth for agentic traffic

title.value: Show HN: Web Bot Auth SDK and SSH Utilty
